note: M2.7 review-packet fixtures (spec/catalogue-report.md §6.9). Bodies are matching.json bodies; licence texts are archived under licence-texts/ and referenced by SHA-256.
derivationRule: A vector is hand-derived when both of these hold: (a) Judgments are written by a person. Every judgment the contract leaves to a reader is written by a person from the contract text. That covers the token boundaries, classes and texts; inserted tokens; the outcome status; and the error code and the position of the defect. For matching vectors it also covers which regions match, and the outcome. (b) Arithmetic is computed and rechecked. Everything that is pure arithmetic over those judgments is computed by the specification's own checker or builder, which is not an implementation under test. That covers byte spans located from the hand-written token texts, SHA-256 hashes, window selection, fingerprints, digests and canonical bytes. At least one independent recomputation, by a clean-room reviewer or a second checker, confirms it. A vector whose lexical layer was first produced by a tool and then reviewed is not hand-derived, and must be labelled otherwise. Applied to these fixtures: each packet's origin kind, side, region, package and commit, each rejection's corrupted field and expected verdict (schema or semantic), and the archived licence texts are written by hand from spec/catalogue-report.md section 6.9. Region keys and artifact, body and licence-text digests are copied or computed by build_gates.py from matching.json bodies, and check_gates.py recomputes the bodies and re-checks every packet.

valid.description: Own-origin region: the GO_SUM region found in a larger host is the reference project's own code at a recorded commit.
Vendored dependency region (vendor control class): the vendored file matches itself; the packet names the package and the digest of the archived licence text.
The same vendored region under the vendor catalogue, where it is common-only: a common-only region is still referenceable.

Historical copy: the loop was copied from an earlier version of the reference at a recorded commit, under the licence then in force. Whether the copy was permitted is a rights conclusion outside the record.
